text.p: Here are the highlights of stories in the Danish press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

--- A new report on organized crime in Denmark made by the Danish police shows that it is slight compared to other countries. None of the large international crime organizations such as the Italian mafia, South American cocaine cartels or the Russian mafia have gained a foothold in Denmark so far.

--- Denmark's exports of agricultural products increased by 4.4 percent in the first six months of 1996 compared to the same period last year. EU export subsidies included, Denmark exported agriproducts worth 25.1 billion crowns in the first six months of 1996, 1.1 billion more than in the same period last year.

--- Months' work on unveiling a large smuggling ring in Denmark has lead to the confiscation of 9,000 pills of the drug ecstasy. The find is the largest ever in Denmark and the pills are said to be worth 1.5 million crowns on the market.

--- For the second year in a row Copenhagen Airport has been named the third best airport in the world, after Singapore and Schiphol in Amsterdam, by the Hong-Kong magazine Business Traveller which lists the best airports in the world every year.
--- Danish abbatoirs are now being exported to the Philippines where close to 80 small but advanced slaughterhouses are to be built by the Danish company Intercool Food Technology A/S.
